message.content: {"summary":"You set out the scenario clearly, naming the key stakeholders and linking the ethical issues to engineering design and organisational pressure. Your report is well organised, with a clear for-and-against discussion that leads to a conclusion. To reach the next level, strengthen the reasoning behind your conclusion, respond to the counterarguments you raise, and support your claims with more varied, complete evidence and visuals.","next_steps":["Rebut the competitor argument directly, explaining why a rival's decision does not make shipping ethical. Avoid relying on marketing articles, such as the Apple source, for claims about engineering-release ethics.","Build an explicit decision framework for when a defective product may ship, such as weighing severity of harm, likelihood, disclosure and mitigation. Use it to derive your recommendation for Rachel and for other stakeholders, rather than asserting the conclusion after the Volkswagen case.","Add more scholarly and quantitative sources, cite every claim such as fines, and complete every reference entry with author, title, date and URL. Include at least one figure or table, such as a stakeholder table or decision flowchart, to support your discussion."],"criteria":{"C1":"You identify several ethical issues, including public safety, professional integrity, transparency and commercial pressure, and link them to server design and your organisation's context. Naming Rachel, her company, the chip supplier and the health department, and recognising indirect end-users, shows a good understanding of who is affected. Keep this breadth as you develop the later sections.","C2":"Your discussion weighs arguments for and against shipping and reaches a clear conclusion. The argument that a competitor would ship anyway is presented without critique, so it needs a rebuttal explaining why a rival's choice does not justify shipping. Guidance for stakeholders beyond Rachel, such as the chip supplier and health department, would add depth to your recommendations.","C3":"Your for-and-against structure makes the report easy to follow, and your conclusion not to ship follows from the discussion. The argument would be more compelling if the conclusion were derived from an explicit decision framework for when defective products may be shipped. Analyse the chip supplier and health department as decision-makers to make your stakeholder analysis systematic.","C4":"You support your arguments with two external case studies, Volkswagen and the medication error, and a professional code, which give useful qualitative evidence. For 1500 words, you need more sources, including scholarly ethics literature, and any quantitative claims need citations. Check that clause 2.3b fits Rachel's situation, as it concerns competence whereas her constraint is time and resourcing.","C5":"Your sections are clearly signposted and the prose is mostly fluent. Proofread for slips such as 'benefits of could' and 'have her company might go under', and correct the 'DICUSSION' heading. The report has no figures or tables, so adding a simple stakeholder table or decision flowchart would strengthen your discussion. Make reference entries consistent and complete."}}
